questions.enonce_markdown:
**(i)** A sample of $n$ independent observations is taken from a normal population with mean 74 and variance 36.

(a) State the distribution of the sample mean, $\bar{X}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
For a sample of size $n$ from $N(\mu, \sigma^2)$, the sample mean satisfies $\bar{X} \sim N\!\left(\mu,\ \dfrac{\sigma^2}{n}\right)$ (exactly, because the parent population is normal).

**$\bar{X} \sim N\!\left(74,\ \dfrac{36}{n}\right)$**, with standard error $\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{n}}$.
themes: sampling distribution of the mean statistics

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Given that $P(\bar{X} > 75) = 0.282$, find the value of $n$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Standardise using $Z = \dfrac{\bar{X} - 74}{6/\sqrt{n}} \sim N(0, 1)$:

$$P(\bar{X} > 75) = P\!\left(Z > \frac{75 - 74}{6/\sqrt{n}}\right) = P\!\left(Z > \frac{\sqrt{n}}{6}\right) = 0.282$$

$$P\!\left(Z < \frac{\sqrt{n}}{6}\right) = 1 - 0.282 = 0.718$$

From the tables, $\Phi(0.57) = 0.7157$ and $\Phi(0.58) = 0.7190$, so $0.718$ corresponds to $z \approx 0.577$:

$$\frac{\sqrt{n}}{6} = 0.577 \;\Longrightarrow\; \sqrt{n} = 3.46 \;\Longrightarrow\; n = 11.99 \approx 12$$

**$n = 12$.** (Check: $\dfrac{\sqrt{12}}{6} = 0.5774$ and $P(Z > 0.5774) = 0.282$.)
themes: sampling distribution of the mean statistics

questions.enonce_markdown: **(ii)** The masses of tubers of yam harvested from a certain farm are normally distributed with mean 145 grams and standard deviation 9 grams. A random sample of 100 yams tubers selected from the farm is found to have a mean mass of 140 grams. Stating clearly, the null and alternative hypotheses, test, at the 5% level of significance whether the mean mass of the yam tubers is reduced.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Hypotheses** ($\mu$ = true mean mass of a yam tuber):

$$H_0: \mu = 145 \text{ g} \qquad H_1: \mu < 145 \text{ g} \quad \text{(one-tailed test, since a reduction is suspected)}$$

**Test statistic.** The population is normal with known $\sigma = 9$, so under $H_0$

$$\bar{X} \sim N\!\left(145,\ \frac{9^2}{100}\right), \qquad \text{standard error} = \frac{9}{\sqrt{100}} = 0.9$$

$$z = \frac{\bar{x} - \mu}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}} = \frac{140 - 145}{0.9} = -5.56$$

**Critical value.** For a one-tailed test at the 5% level, the critical region is $z < -1.645$.

**Decision.** $-5.56 < -1.645$, so the result lies in the critical region (the probability of a sample mean this low is $P(Z < -5.56) \approx 1.4 \times 10^{-8}$, far below $0.05$). We reject $H_0$.

**Conclusion:** at the 5% level of significance there is sufficient evidence that the mean mass of the yam tubers has been reduced.
themes: sampling distribution of the mean statistics
